slides.say: The operation diamond is defined for every number a. Diamond of a is equal to a squared minus four a. Diamond of six is equal to what?
So we have a rule, and we need to use it on the number six. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, first by putting six straight into the rule, and then by simplifying the rule before we use it.
at: use it on the number six

slides.say: [short pause] Remember what the rule means. Whatever goes into the diamond takes the place of a, in every spot where a appears. Here a appears in two spots, in a squared and in four a. So let's write the same template again, and put six in every spot.
Careful here. A lot of students put six only into a squared, and forget the four a. But six goes into every a.
So diamond of six is six squared minus four times six. Six squared is thirty-six. Four times six is twenty-four. Thirty-six minus twenty-four is twelve.
So diamond of six is twelve, and choice number two is our answer. Thirty-six, choice number one, is only the first part of the rule.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to simplify the rule first, and only then put the number in. Both parts of a squared minus four a have an a in them. So we can take a out as a common factor. a squared minus four a is a times, in brackets, a minus four. Let's check it. a times a is a squared, and a times negative four is negative four a.
at: a squared minus four a is a times

slides.say: Now put six in. Six times, in brackets, six minus four. Six minus four is two, and six times two is twelve. Again twelve, choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
